faq.a: An array of objects works best — each object becomes a row and the union of all keys becomes the columns. A single object is treated as a one-row table, and missing keys become empty cells.

faq.a: They are written into the cell as compact JSON text, so no data is lost. Cells containing commas, quotes, or line breaks are automatically quoted per the CSV standard.

whenNotToUse: Deeply nested or irregular JSON (arrays of arrays, mixed primitives and objects) will produce a flattened approximation — reshape the data first if you need a precise table.
It converts in the browser, so extremely large JSON files (tens of MB) may be slow or hit memory limits — use a command-line tool like jq for those.
